title: Etale logification comparison and characteristic geometry
statement: Let $X$ be locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], $P$ a Zariski prelog sheaf and $Z$ a Zariski log structure [def-trf-zariski-log-structure]. Suppose $z$ is a normalized unit-pushout presentation universal for Zariski log maps. Let $E$ and $F$ be normalized prelog inverse images of $P$ and $Z$, and let $l$ and $n$ be normalized etale logification presentations of $E$ and $F$, universal for etale log maps [def-trf-prelog-logification-data]. There exist a characteristic monoid sheaf $H$ and normalized quotient presentation $h$ of $L$. The canonical comparison between the logifications of $F$ and $E$ is an isomorphism, fixing the prelog inclusions and structural maps. The stalk of $E$ is $P_x$ and the stalk of $L$ is the pushout for the composite of beta_x with the canonical unit-reflecting local map $O_x\to O_{\bar x}$, with all formulas on pair germs and units as in EtaleStalks. The characteristic stalk of $H$ is the Associates quotient of that pushout, normalized on pair germs for every normalized local map and inverse-image stalk isomorphism. The three presentations l,n,h restrict to every slice with exactly the restricted maps. Existence and universal properties of the logifications and inverse images are hypotheses, not conclusions.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites] and [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact], the normalized inverse images implement the monoid inverse-image adjunction. Restricting an etale log structure to opens gives a Zariski log structure. The assumed three universal properties identify compatible Hom functors for N and L; extending their canonical maps in both directions and applying uniqueness gives inverse isomorphisms. The adjunction constructs the middle map E to F and verifies all four normalization equations.

proof.text: Use openness of etale maps [def-weil-etale-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. A raw section on image(W) maps to its ordinary germ; conversely use an open pointed neighborhood to represent an ordinary germ. W to image(W) identifies the second composite with the identity. Filteredness and the elementwise colimit equality criterion justify the refinements. The geometric-stalk sheafification theorem, with monoid sheafification, carries this identification to E and gives the structural compatibility.

proof.text: Construct the canonical map from ordinary local functions to the etale stalk on open germs. A function becoming a unit becomes a unit on a pointed etale neighborhood by [lem-trf-filtered-ring-log-pushout], hence has nonzero residue value at x by [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-residue-field]. Shrink to its basic open by [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function]. This proves reflection of units. Apply [lem-trf-filtered-varying-prelog-pushout] to compute the logification stalk, using the inverse-image stalk identification and the same inverse unit submonoid. The pair formulas and the unique lift of units give EtaleStalks.

proof.text: Quotient L sectionwise by monoid units and sheafify. Lifting unit germs and finite equality witnesses at one stage proves that its stalk is Associates(L_t). Sheafification preserves this geometric stalk. Combine the normalized log stalk map with the quotient map to get the required formula, for every normalized rho and eP; these maps agree on all raw germs and are therefore unique.
